title: Who shares the world's rivers? 313 basins, 19 countries on the Danube, and why nobody agrees on the longest river
excerpt: 313 river basins cross a border. They drain 47% of the world's land outside Antarctica and hold 45% of its people. I mapped them, measured the great rivers on one map, and found the longest river depends on who holds the ruler.
seo_description: A map of the world's 313 shared river basins and the countries in each, the longest rivers measured on one map, and who depends on water from upstream.
header_alt: Title card reading 'Who shares the world's rivers?' in dark ink on pale paper, with the number 313 in blue and the line: river basins cross a border; they drain 47% of the land outside Antarctica and hold 45% of the world's people. Beside it, a world map of the shared basins shaded from pale green to deep indigo by the number of countries sharing each, darkest over the Danube, Nile, Niger and Congo, with blue rivers.
